newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Tadiran exports up, local sales down.
newsitem.headline: Tadiran exports up, local sales down.

text.p: Israel's largest electronics company Tadiran Ltd said on Wednesday that the first quarter of 1997 was characterised by a sharp increase in exports and a significant decrease in domestic sales.
This was especially notable at its subsidiary Tadiran Telecommunications, which reported sharply lower sales to Bezeq Israel Telecom.
"This trend was expected and constitutes a basic assumption of our plans for 1997," Tadiran said in a statement. "This trend...prevented a strong negative impact on the first quarter's results."

Adverse economic conditions and difficulties in the export market hurt Tadiran Appliances for the second consecutive quarter "as shown by the losses resulting from a significant decline in sales", the statement said.
The parent company reported an $8.4 million increase in sales in the first quarter to $277.8 million.

Exports rose by 31 percent to $155.2 million and comprise 55.9 percent of total sales, against 44 percent in the year earlier quarter. Commercial export sales grew by 73.4 percent to $90.5 million from $52.2 million, principally of telecommunications and vehicle location products.
Gross profit as a percentage of sales rose due to increased turnover in the military communications sector and efficiencies resulting from workforce reduction.
Net research and development expenses in the first quarter increased to $16.8 million from $14.1 million.
Selling expenses rose 10.8 percent to $24.9 million primarily due to commission payments and other marketing expenses to promote increased export.

General and administrative expenses totalled $17 million, up from $13 million a year earlier. The increase was mainly due to the reversal of $2.3 million in allowance for doubtful accounts in the corresponding period.

The increase in expenses hurt operating income, which fell to $18.3 million from $23.7 million. The decrease in the telecommunications segment was partly offset by a $2.9 million increase in the communications segment and a $2 million rise in the computer software segment.
During the period the company recorded $5.1 million in capital gains, mainly from the sale of 51 percent of Tadiran Information Systems to IBM, against $0.1 million a year earlier.
Net income fell to $15.5 million from $18.6 million.
The company's order backlog grew by $87.6 million from the end of 1996 to $908 million.
